assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and wage setting, and the microfounded New Keynesian framework are the standard basis for modern monetary policy analysis. They shape central-bank practice, including policy rules, inflation targeting and the use of DSGE models. The contribution is both conceptual and practical, and it is of very broad scientific and policy significance.
assessment.attribution: The cluster is crowded. Calvo's time-dependent pricing (1983) and Taylor's staggered contracts and policy rule are the foundational pieces. Woodford's synthesis supplies the welfare-theoretic and policy framework. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are important for estimation, empirics and medium-scale models, but a limit of three means leaving out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of validation and use in central banks. The 2022 inflation episode revived debate about the framework, but it has not undermined the core contributions. Timing is mature and, arguably, overdue.
uncertainties: Who belongs in the three is contestable: Gali, Gertler and Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans have strong claims.
Whether the committee prefers a narrower, more theoretical or more empirical-VAR-based award.
Post-2008 and post-2021 critiques of the framework could weigh on the assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection changed international trade by moving the unit of analysis from industries to firms. It explains exporter premia, within-industry reallocation and a new channel for gains from trade. The Melitz (2003) model is a workhorse across trade, macro and development, and Helpman's broader trade theory is foundational.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the central originator of the heterogeneous-firm model. Helpman is a central architect of the new trade theory and of the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extension. Redding, Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are close contributors on empirical and quantitative approaches, so some overlap with the quantitative trade cluster exists.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of extensive empirical and quantitative follow-up. Krugman's 2008 prize covered earlier new trade theory, but this contribution is distinct and well confirmed.
uncertainties: Overlap with B003 and B041 (Helpman appears in several candidates) could split support.
Bernard, Eaton and Kortum could be viewed as co-originators of heterogeneous-firm trade.
Quantitative work suggests the welfare gains from selection may be smaller than first claimed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints and asset prices amplify and propagate shocks. This became the core mechanism in the macro-financial literature and in thinking about the 2008 crisis. The result is deep, general and policy relevant.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear joint originators of the credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the financial accelerator and its empirical and quantitative development, but Bernanke's earlier Nobel in 2022 partly covered that strand.
assessment.maturity: Close to three decades of citation and use, with strong confirmation after 2008. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the contribution as one paper plus follow-ups or as a broad body of work.
The 2022 prize for banks and financial crises overlaps thematically.
Empirical identification of collateral channels is harder to confirm than the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income series built from tax data, the study of wealth concentration and the associated measurement agenda changed research and public debate about inequality. The measurement contribution is major and has produced a large body of follow-up work and datasets, such as the World Inequality Database.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-income series work (2003), and Zucman is a major contributor on wealth and offshore holdings. Atkinson's earlier work is a precursor, and Atkinson is deceased. The theoretical interpretation of capital and inequality in Piketty's later work is more contested than the measurement.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of measurement. The data work is established, but the causal and theoretical claims about r > g are contested. Zucman's offshore-wealth estimates are more recent and remain under scrutiny.
uncertainties: The measurement of distributional national accounts and of wealth tax data is disputed.
Choice between a two-person and a three-person award, given Zucman's recency.
Saez also appears in B007, so credit may be split across candidates.
Concerns that policy advocacy shapes perceptions of the scientific contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) quantified how misallocation of inputs across firms can explain a large share of cross-country TFP differences. It established a disciplined, widely used framework in macro-development and growth, and it links micro data to aggregate income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the central authors of the quantification approach. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) are important co-originators of the misallocation idea, and the three-person limit may leave out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of influence. Measurement challenges, such as the role of measurement error and markups, remain, so the contribution is influential but not fully settled.
uncertainties: Measurement error and markup heterogeneity affect the size of the estimated gains.
Restuccia and Rogerson have a plausible claim to co-credit.
The 2025 prize on innovation-led growth and the 2024 prize on institutions may reduce appetite for another growth-related award soon.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based approach to technological change and the China-shock evidence reshaped understanding of labor-market polarization, trade exposure and local adjustment. The work combines credible empirical design with conceptual framing and is highly policy relevant.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the core authors of the China-shock evidence. Autor, Katz and Murnane developed the task framework, and Acemoglu's task-based theory is a central related contribution. The grouping splits credit between two distinct strands, and Katz's role is substantial.
assessment.maturity: A decade of replication and debate on the China shock, with generally robust local effects but dispute about the magnitude of the aggregate impact. The task framework has been confirmed more broadly.
uncertainties: Exposure-based designs have been criticised for inference and for external validity.
Acemoglu's earlier recognition and the overlap with the task-based theory complicate the credit.
Whether to emphasise the task framework or the China-shock evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how economists think about what can be learned from data under weak assumptions. Manski's bounds approach is foundational for credible inference and informs treatment-effect, selection and policy analysis. It is a deep methodological contribution with broad consequences.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator of the bounds approach. Tamer is a leading developer of moment-inequality econometrics, and Molinari has been central to later inference theory. The grouping is coherent, but Manski's priority dominates.
assessment.maturity: Manski's seminal work dates from about 1989 onward, so it is long confirmed. The later econometric-inference development is still ongoing, and Manski's age adds some timing urgency.
uncertainties: The empirical adoption in applied work is narrower than the methodological influence.
The committee might prefer to recognise the econometric inference contributions separately.
Competing econometrics clusters (B023, B024, B043) could split support.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the open economy, exchange-rate dynamics, and the exchange-rate disconnect puzzles established the modern framework for international macroeconomics. The framework underlies standard analysis of current-account dynamics and policy.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the principal authors of the standard graduate treatment and the New Open Economy Macroeconomics, with the Redux model as a key piece. Rogoff also appears in B027 (with Reinhart), so credit is split across several lines. Other contributors, such as Dornbusch and Svensson, are deceased or less central.
assessment.maturity: Established over three decades, though the empirical puzzles are still unresolved. The theoretical framework has been broadly adopted.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is viewed as a synthesis and textbook rather than a discovery.
Rogoff's name across several candidates may dilute his claim.
Unresolved empirical puzzles lower confidence in the core mechanisms.
